claims.text: Adding high-angle grain-boundary energy and grain-size-distribution parameters to a predictive framework will improve identification of low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys.
Single-phase HEAs with ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layers will have lower phonon thermal conductivity than traditional empirical approaches predict.
CoCrFeMnNi is a single-phase high-entropy alloy that can exhibit inverse Hall-Petch behavior in ultra-high vacuum.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi material can be coarse-grained and comparatively soft.
Thermal or mechanical processing can promote dynamic amorphization and create ultra-nanocrystalline surface layers in candidate HEAs.
Inert or ultra-high-vacuum environments mitigate oxidation and mixed metal-oxide-film formation.
Specific annealing or mechanical-deformation conditions drive formation of a dynamic amorphous surface layer.
Grain size and high-angle grain-boundary energy are relevant parameters of the dynamic-amorphization model.
Dynamic amorphization is associated with ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface features and nanoporosity.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer increases grain-boundary density and structural disorder.
The increased grain-boundary density and structural disorder enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces phonon thermal conductivity.
HEAs selected by the augmented approach will have measured phonon thermal conductivity at least 30% lower than values estimated by conventional predictions.
Established empirical thermal-conductivity correlations ignore dynamic-amorphization effects and grain-boundary contributions.
The approach is applicable only to single-phase HEAs synthesized under controlled inert conditions that enable inverse Hall-Petch behavior.
The approach may not apply to multiphase alloys or alloys processed under oxidizing conditions.
The claimed 30% improvement in prediction accuracy is provisional and requires testing across compositions and processing conditions.
STEM and diffraction methods can determine grain-size distribution and high-angle grain-boundary energy for the proposed benchmark.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can determine the phonon contribution to thermal conductivity in the proposed HEAs.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines 30% as measured conductivity being lower than a conventional prediction, whereas the uncertainty field calls it a 30% improvement in prediction accuracy. These are different quantities: demonstrating lower conductivity does not by itself demonstrate improved predictive accuracy.
The rule treats lack of statistical significance and failure to reach a 30% effect-size threshold as equivalent, although statistical significance and effect magnitude are distinct criteria.
